content.text:
---
name: "canvas"
description: "Draws on a tldraw canvas run from a local app, which the user edits too, with low-fidelity screen mockups, storage cylinders, arrows and free text, and exports it as an SVG. Use when the user asks for a mockup, a sketch or a diagram laid out in space, or when another skill loads it to draw. Mermaid stays the choice for diagrams that live as text in a document, such as sequence, state, ER and flowcharts."
argument-hint: "<what to draw>"
---
Load mahou:basics first. Then read `.mahou/canvas.md` if present.

# Canvas

## Documents

A canvas is one document, `<name>.tldr.json`, in a folder a loading skill names along with the name. When the user types the skill, the folder is `canvas/` in the change's scratch folder and the document is named after what it draws. A folder can hold several documents.

- `<name>.tldr.json` is the document. The server holds it while the canvas runs and saves every edit to it, from any tab. Its `canvasVersion` names its format.
- `<name>.svg` is its export, next to it.
- `mockups/` holds the mockups every document in the folder can draw, one `<kind>.tsx` file each. A mockup is the content of the canvas's custom `mock` shape, for anything the stock tldraw shapes do not draw, such as a screen. Its file exports `mockup`, a `MockDefinition<Props>` from `@canvas/MockShape`: its natural width, its default props and a function that renders them. The natural width can also be a function of the props, for a mockup whose views have different widths. A click that changes the natural width resizes the shape by the same ratio, so the drawing keeps its scale. The canvas draws a mockup with no natural width, such as the built-in `area`, at the shape's own size instead of scaling it, so its border and label keep their size however large the shape is. A `mock` shape's `data` is merged over the defaults, so a shape passes only what differs, such as `{ kind: 'login', data: { state: 'error' } }`. A `mock` shape draws its kind at the natural width and scales the drawing to the shape's size, so one mockup renders at any shape size. Adding, changing or removing a file in `mockups/` redraws the shapes in every open tab without reloading the page.

## Running it

`scripts/canvas.sh` runs the app over one document. Pass it the document's path:

- `start` installs the app on first run, starts a detached server for the document on the first free port from 5190 and prints the URL to give the user. A document that already has a server gets its URL back. Each document has its own server, so several canvases run at once, in one project or in several; `CANVAS_PORT` picks the port instead. It refuses a document saved in an older format and names the `migrate` command.
- `watch` prints one line per event: `click` for each "Send to Agent" click, and `voice: <message>` for each voice message, with the shapes selected when it was sent.
- `export` writes `<name>.svg`.
- `texts` prints every canvas text and arrow label, one per line.
- `migrate` brings an older document to the current format, keeping the original as `<name>.tldr.json.bak`. Run it with the server stopped. When it warns that a mockup received a variant string, rewrite that mockup to read its props from `data`.
- `stop` stops the document's own server and leaves every other canvas running.

Edits to the app under `scripts/app/` reach the running canvas only after a restart, because `start` copies the app into the cache. Run `stop` and then `start`, and reload the open tabs.

Build and edit the canvas from scripts run with `agent-browser` in your own tab, opened once on `<URL>?user=Agent` and kept open, so the user sees your cursor under that name. Every tab edits the same document live: your changes appear in the user's tab as you make them, and theirs in yours. The page exposes `window.editor`, `window.tldraw` with `createShapeId` and `toRichText`, and `window.canvas` with `notes()`, `step(at, change, pause?)` and the drawing helpers below.

Draw in steps the user can follow. A script's changes reach the other tabs together, so a script that draws everything at once shows the user only the finished result. Run each element as an awaited `canvas.step`: it moves your cursor to `at` (a shape id or a page point, or `null` to stay), applies `change`, and waits `pause` milliseconds, 500 by default. One step per shape, arrow or move, in the order a person would draw them: follow the flow the drawing explains, and join each element to what it connects to as soon as both are on the canvas, so the drawing grows as one connected piece and never as all the boxes first and all the arrows last.

- An area goes first, before what it holds.
- After the first element, each new element is followed right away by the arrow that joins it to what is already drawn, then by that arrow's label if it has one.
- A note goes right after the element it describes, and its arrow right after the note.

Draw a large batch in one script instead, without `canvas.step`, when a change creates or redraws many shapes at once, such as every tree rebuilt from a revised record. Stepping through hundreds of shapes makes the user wait for a drawing they will read only once it is finished.

Check every change with a screenshot, saved under a new file name each time, since reading a path you read before can show the earlier image.

## Helpers

The helpers load with the page, so they are back after agent-browser relaunches its browser and you reopen the tab. Each helper takes a shape name and builds the shape id from it with `id(name)`, so one name reaches the same shape through every helper. Each helper that creates a shape runs as one `step`, so the user sees it arrive, and takes an optional `pause`.

The helpers keep the layout with one rule. A shape belongs to the innermost area that holds its top edge. When no area holds it, it belongs to the lowest area of its column whose top edge is above the shape's top edge. An area nested inside another area does not count in that case, so a shape placed under a nested area belongs to the area around it. To place a new shape inside a nested area, pass `into: '<area>'` to the helper that creates the shape. The area grows to hold the shape's top edge before the helper creates the shape. `flow` does the same for a column of shapes. When a shape's height changes, the shapes under it in the same area move by the same amount. The shape's area grows or shrinks to keep a 40-unit margin under the area's lowest shape. An area that sits strictly between another area's left and right edges belongs to that area, even when the inner area starts below the outer area's bottom edge. Growing the outer area does not move the nested area, and the outer area grows to hold the nested area. When an area's height changes, the areas under it in the column move, each with its shapes and the areas nested in it. A nested area that grows moves only the areas under it inside the same outer area; the outer area then grows and moves the areas under it. Place a new shape under the last one in its area, and the helpers grow the area and move the areas under it.

| Helper | What it does |
|---|---|
| `id(name)` | The shape id for a name. |
| `bounds(name)` | The shape's page bounds. |
| `plain(name)` | Reads the shape's text back as plain text, with its line breaks. Use it to edit a text in place instead of keeping a copy of the text in a script. |
| `area(name, { x, y, w, h, label, focus? }, pause?)` | Creates an `area` with its label and sends it to the back. With a name that exists, replaces the label, such as a branch's status, keeping the focus it had. `focus: true` focuses the area, as `focus` does, on creation or along with the label change. |
| `focus(name, pause?)` | Focuses the named `area`: its border turns solid red while every other area's stays grey and dashed. Only one area is focused at a time, so every other area loses the focus. With `null`, clears the focus from every area. |
| `text(name, { x, y, w, text, mono?, size?, into? }, pause?)` | Creates a text of a fixed width, in the hand font or in monospace with `mono: true`. With a name that exists, replaces the text, and moves or widens it when `x`, `y` or `w` are given. With `into`, the named area grows to hold the new shape before the helper creates the shape, so the shape belongs to that area. |
| `card(name, { x, y, w, text, color?, dash?, fill?, mono?, into? }, pause?)` | Creates a rectangle holding a text and fits its height to the text. The rectangle is violet with a semi fill by default. Use it for a question card, a summary box (`color: 'grey', fill: 'solid'`) or a monospace table (`mono: true`). With a name that exists, replaces the text and fits the height to it again. With `into`, the named area grows to hold the new shape before the helper creates the shape, so the shape belongs to that area. |
| `box(name, { x, y, w, h, text, geo?, color?, fill?, dash?, into? }, pause?)` | Creates a diagram node of a fixed size with its text centred. `geo` is `rectangle` (the default), `ellipse` or `cloud`. Use it for the parts of a diagram, coloured by the deployable they belong to. Use `card` for text that sets its own height. With a name that exists, replaces the text. With `into`, the named area grows to hold the new shape before the helper creates the shape, so the shape belongs to that area. |
| `arrow(name, from, to, { text?, bend?, labelPosition?, color?, dash? }, pause?)` | Creates an arrow bound to the centres of the shapes `from` and `to`, so the arrow follows either shape when that shape moves. With a name that exists, changes only the options given. |
| `mermaid(name, { x, y, source }, pause?)` | Creates a `mermaid` shape and sizes it to the diagram's `viewBox`, one canvas unit per diagram unit, once the diagram has rendered. With a name that exists, replaces the source and sizes the shape again. |
| `mock(name, { x, y, w?, kind, data, into? }, pause?)` | Creates a `mock` shape of the given kind with its `data`, 520 units wide unless `w` sets another width, and fits its height to the content. With a name that exists, replaces the `data` and fits the height again. With `into`, the named area grows to hold the new shape first. |
| `note(name, { x, y, w, text }, pause?)` | Creates or updates an Agent note, a grey dashed `card` labelled "Agent". The helper adds the label, so `text` holds only the message. |
| `followUp(name, { summary, note, question? })` | Fills a card with its follow-up under the card's own text: a summary box, an Agent note and, when given, the next question as a card. Replaces the parts of an earlier follow-up. The parts move with the card. |
| `fit(name)` | Zooms to the shape and sets its height from what it holds: a card or a note from its text and its follow-up, a `mermaid` shape from its diagram's `viewBox`, any other `mock` from its `data-root` element scaled from the mockup's natural width, an `area` from its lowest shape. Returns the height, or `null` when the shape isn't drawn. |
| `resize(name, { h?, w? })` | Sets a shape's height or width. A new width on an area widens every top-level area in its column, the areas that share the resized area's left edge. Areas nested inside them keep their width. Each shape to the right of the column moves right by as much as the column area beside it grew, so a shape beside a narrower area clears that area's new edge. A shape beside no column area moves by as much as the resized area grew. |
| `move(name, { x?, y? }, pause?)` | Moves a shape to a new position. A card's follow-up parts move with the card. An area moves with its shapes and its nested areas. The area the shape leaves and the area the shape lands in fit their height again. Move shapes with `move` rather than through `editor.updateShape`, which leaves parts behind and fits no area. |
| `flow(area, names, { top?, gap? })` | Lays the named shapes out one under another inside an area, from `top` (60 units under the area's top edge by default) with `gap` between them (30 by default). The area grows to hold them before they move, so no shape lands past the area's bottom edge, where the next area down would take the shape. |
| `classificationTree(name, spec, { x, y })` | Draws one test branch whole, in one batch, as an `area` labelled `spec.label`: the root as a blue box, each classification as a violet box joined to the root by a line with no arrowheads, each partition as a green box joined the same way, and the matrix under them. A matrix row has a narrow `★` column on the far left (`★` when `isNew: true`, blank otherwise), its id and summary next to it, a filled dot under each partition it picks, and its expected outcome, kind and setup on the right. A row with `manual: true` is orange. Grey dotted lines run between the rows, after the `★` column, and down each partition's column; the dropped rows (`Dropped: …`), deleted tests (`Deleted: …`) and the note sit in grey below the matrix when present. `spec` holds `label`, `root`, `classifications` (each a `name` and its `partitions` as `[key, label]` pairs), `rows` (each `id`, `summary`, `picks` as one partition key per classification, `expected`, `kind`, `setup?`, `manual?` and `isNew?`), `dropped?`, `deleted?` and `note?`. With a name that exists, draws the branch again in place under fresh ids. |

For example, a question with its follow-up in an open area:

```js
await canvas.card('q4', { x, y, w: 1160, text: '❓ Q4 · <title>\n\n<body>' })
await canvas.followUp('q4', { summary: 'Summary · Q4 so far\n\n<settled and findings>', note: '<how the answer was read>' })
await canvas.note('n2', { text: '<the next reading>' })
```

A session that needs more than these writes its own helpers as scripts in the canvas folder, loads them into the tab, and loads them again after a relaunch.

## Mockups

Mockups import the shared pieces from `@canvas/kit`: `theme`, with the ink, paper, colours, hand font and a sketched border, and `Browser`, a browser window around a screen. Five kinds are built in: `cylinder`, whose data is `{ title, caption }`; `area`, a rounded dashed region whose data is `{ label, isFocus }`, which draws a solid red border while focused, for grouping the shapes inside a part, used instead of a frame and sent to the back; `mermaid`, whose data is `{ source }`, a mermaid diagram drawn in the canvas's ink and hand font; `code-snippet`, a fragment of code or config; and `blank-screen`. Use a `mermaid` shape for a finished diagram that will change little. Draw an exploration or an unsettled diagram with tldraw shapes, which are easier to change. A `mermaid` shape scales its diagram to fit and keeps the diagram's proportions. Create it with `mermaid(name, …)`, which sizes it to the diagram. Write and validate the source with superpowers:mermaid. The shape draws with pele, the renderer superpowers:mermaid's PNG comes from, so it looks like that PNG.

Use a `code-snippet` to show a change to a file, such as a config the user has not seen. Its data is `{ file, tag, lines, gutterNotes, highlight, view, expanded }`. Each line is `{ text, mark, note }`, where `mark` is `same`, `add`, `remove` or `gap`, and a `gap` line draws `⋯` for the code left out. With `gutterNotes`, each line's `note` sits beside it, starting at the line's height without making the line taller. A note longer than two lines shows its first two lines and a "more…" link that expands it. `highlight` is a list of `{ pattern, color }` rules that the snippet tries in order at each position of a line. It defaults to JS/TS; pass rules for another language. `view` is `unified`, with `+` and `−` marks, or `split`, with the old code on the left and the new on the right. A toggle in the header switches between the two views. `view` is `code` for a file shown as it is rather than as a change. In that view the snippet has no toggle, no `+` and `−` marks and no mark colours, only the code with its highlighting.

Keep them low fidelity: the hand font, sketched borders, and grey bars for text that does not matter.

When the screen has a prototype, copy the mockup from it: the same parts, the same states and the same copy, translated into the language the canvas is written in. A state that is its own view in the prototype is its own mockup on the canvas.

- **Size a mock to its content** when the content's height depends on its data. Give the mockup's root element a `data-root` attribute, and lay it out from the top with no bottom edge. Zoom your tab to the shape, and once the shape has rendered, set the shape's `h` to the root's `offsetHeight` times the shape's width over the mockup's natural width. The canvas renders only the shapes on screen, so a shape measured off screen has no root element. Its `h` then drops to a few units while its content still draws at full size, and every arrow bound to the shape ends at its top edge. `fit(name)` does all of this, and `mock(name, …)` calls it after creating the shape.
- **Make a mockup interactive** when the user needs to switch what it shows, such as a view or a collapsed part. Mark each element that takes a click with `data-interactive`; tldraw keeps every other click for selecting and moving the shape. `render` receives `update(patch)` as its second argument, which merges the patch into the shape's `data`, so the canvas saves the change and every tab shows it. While the shape is on screen, the canvas keeps the shape's height equal to the height of its `data-root` element, so a click that grows or shrinks the content resizes the shape.
- **A shape's `data` holds only JSON.** An `undefined` anywhere inside it fails validation and crashes every open tab; write `null` instead.

## Drawing

- **Notes are free text.** A short sentence with an arrow to the spot it describes. Never a sticky note, since sticky notes are the user's messages.
- **Arrows point at an element's centre**, so they follow when the element moves. An arrow points at a specific spot only when it means that spot: a button, an option, a row.
- **To point at a spot inside a mock**, such as one card in a mockup that draws several, give that element an attribute that names it. Read the element's bounds in the page, convert its corner or edge to a page point with `editor.screenToPage`, and bind the arrow's end to the mock with that point as a `normalizedAnchor`, `isPrecise: true` and `isExact: true`. Without `isExact` the arrow stops at the mock's outer edge.
- Text is black, arrow labels included, and written in tldraw's default font, the hand font (`font: 'draw'`): prose, notes, labels and cards alike. Use the monospace font only where the loading skill asks for it, such as a tree of leaves.
- **Draw each kind of part with its own shape.** Draw each of the system's own modules as a rectangle, coloured by the deployable it belongs to. Draw a store as a cylinder, titled with the product that holds the data, such as `<provider> Postgres`, and captioned with the data it holds. Draw an external service as a cloud, the client as an ellipse, and a platform or a deployable as an `area` around its parts.
- **Label each arrow with the payload or the action it carries**, and with the binding, protocol or credential it goes through when that matters.
- **Spread the canvas across columns instead of letting it grow downwards.** Put related parts in the same column, and start a new column to the right for a part unrelated to the existing ones. Give all top-level areas in a column the same width.
- **Lay a flow out left to right.** Put whoever starts it on the left, stores in a column of their own next to the modules that write them, and external services along the far edge. Draw a process as a vertical column of numbered steps, each with the store or service it reaches on the same row, so its arrow runs straight across.
- **Leave room under a title.** Keep the first shape inside an area clear of the area's label.
- **Keep every shape, label and arrow clear of the others.** When a straight arrow would cross a shape or another arrow's label, curve it with `bend` or move its label with `labelPosition`. When labels crowd each other, move the shapes apart.
- **Leave room for each arrow's label.** Place two shapes joined by a labelled arrow 250 to 300 units apart. With a gap of about 100, the label wraps one word per line over the arrow and the shapes. Keep a label to a few words, since it wraps to the width of its gap. Lay the shapes out with these gaps before drawing the first arrow, instead of fixing collisions after the screenshot.
- **When notes around one diagram would send arrows across it**, centre the diagram and place each note on the side nearest the element it points at, stacked in the same order as their targets so no two arrows cross. When arrows or notes still overlap, add space between the elements or above them and move the notes there.
- **Box the parts of one thing with an `area`, never a frame.** When several separate shapes are parts of the same thing, such as the variants of one part or the screens of one sequence, draw a `mock` shape of kind `area` around them. Send it to the back. Shapes that only sit near each other get no area.
- **Resize an area whenever what it holds grows or moves**, so it keeps a margin around its contents.
- **Set `growY: 0` whenever a script sets a geo shape's `h`.** tldraw keeps the `growY` it computed for the earlier size, and the shape stays taller than what it holds. To stack shapes inside a geo shape under its label, read the label's height first: the height of the shape's `.tl-rich-text` element divided by the zoom level.
- **Delete the arrows of the shapes you delete.** An arrow bound to a deleted shape stays on the canvas where it was drawn. After deleting shapes, delete every arrow with fewer than two bindings.
- **Group what moves together.** Each element, or each set of elements that belong together, is one tldraw group with its title, made with `editor.groupShapes`. Group no further than the smallest set that is one cohesive thing. Elements joined by arrows can share a group, such as the steps of one flow. An element that stands on its own gets its own group, even when an arrow joins it to another element. Arrows between two groups stay outside both, so they stay attached at each end when either group moves.

## Working with the user

- **Your tab holds the current state.** Read what you change from `window.editor` right before changing it, since the user may have moved it. Once the user has edited the canvas, never rebuild it; change only the shapes the change touches.
- **Focus the area you are drawing in.** The focused area draws a solid red border instead of the grey dashed one, so the user can follow where your actions are happening. Pass `focus: true` when creating an area you are about to fill, and call `focus(name)` on the existing area when the work moves there. Leave the focus alone for a small adjustment to one shape: change it only when an area becomes where you will draw for a while, and clear it with `focus(null)` when you stop drawing.
- **Talking in the chat.** Say what changed and ask in the reply. The user answers in the chat, by voice, or with sticky notes.
- **Talking on the canvas.** Write what you would say in the chat as an Agent note, a grey dashed rectangle labelled `Agent`, in the part of the canvas it is about. The user answers with sticky notes or by voice. The loading skill says which of the two to use; when it does not, ask the user.
- **Never reuse a deleted shape's id.** Sync sends a deleted shape recreated under its id as an update to the old record, so a new shape of another type under that id fails validation in every open tab.
- **A sticky note on the canvas is a message from the user.** When you give the user the URL, tell them to put a sticky note on the shape they want changed, or to draw an arrow from the note to it. `window.canvas.notes()` returns each note with its targets: the shapes an arrow joins it to, else the shapes it sits on, smallest first. Act on each note, and once it is handled, delete it together with its `arrows` and tell the user.
- **"Send to Agent", or Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on a Mac), notifies that a batch of edits is ready.** The document is already saved. While the canvas is open, keep `canvas.sh watch` running under a monitor that notifies you on every line it prints; each line is a click. A background command that reports only when it exits never tells you about a click, and you never read the user's notes. Do not react to the user's edits between clicks. When the monitor expires, start it again.
- **The mic button, or holding Ctrl+. (Cmd+. on a Mac), sends a voice message.** The user holds it while talking and releases it to send; the browser's speech recognition turns the speech into text, in the browser's language unless the URL carries `?lang=<code>`. The watch prints it as `voice: <message>`, followed by ` | selected: <id> (<type>: "<text>"), …` when the user had shapes selected as they released it, and the document is saved first, as with a click. The selected shapes are what the message's "this" or "here" refers to. Treat it as a message from the user in the chat: answer it, and read the canvas for any notes it refers to. A notification can cut a long voice message short. When a message reads as cut off, read its whole line in the watch monitor's output file before acting on it.

## Export

1. **Unslop the texts.** Collect the output of `canvas.sh texts` and the explanatory texts written inside the mockups the document uses into a file in the change's scratch folder, and run superpowers:unslop over it. When that skill is not installed, say so and continue. Apply the findings that survive verification to the canvas and the mockups.
2. **Export.** Run `canvas.sh export`. The loading skill places the SVG where it needs the image.

## Ending

When the loading skill's work is done, or the user moves on to other work, stop the canvas: run `canvas.sh stop` on the document, stop the monitor running `canvas.sh watch`, and close your `agent-browser` tab.

##### .mahou/wiki/architecture.md
# kurasu: architecture rules

verified: 2026-10-19

Answers how kurasu's backend code is split and which rules its Effect code follows.

## Knowledge

- `packages/core` defines services named after a job (sessions, polls, access, mailer) and their ports. It imports no adapter and nothing from Cloudflare, Alchemy, Drizzle or jose.
- Adapters live outside core: the D1 adapters in `packages/database`, the R2, Email Sending, JWT and Durable Object adapters in `apps/api`. The apps wire the core services to their adapters; packages never import apps.
- Expected failures are typed errors declared with Schema; the code does not catch defects as if they were expected.
- Decode everything that enters at a boundary (a request body, a stored row, a message) with its schema before using it.
- The Worker reads configuration with Effect `Config` where it is built and passes it to the layers as plain values (`Access.layer(webOrigin)`, `JoseSessionTokens(jwtSecret)`). Secrets come from varlock: `.env.schema` declares them and `.env.local`, out of git, holds them. The mail binding and the D1 resource also read two test-only variables, `KURASU_MAIL_ALLOWED_DESTINATIONS` and `KURASU_D1_IMPORT_FILES`, which `.env.schema` declares without a default, so `Config.option` reads them as absent outside the API tests.
- Declare Alchemy resources outside the Worker's runtime path, because a Worker's initialization runs once at deploy and again when the isolate starts. The API Worker builds its HTTP app, with every layer that reads D1, inside `fetch`, because the bindings exist only when the isolate starts (see `alchemy/local-dev`).
- Reads are bounded (a list has a maximum) and paginate by key, not by offset.
- D1 has no transactions: writes that must land together go in one batch.

## Sources

- `.scratch/aula-virtual/program-design/kurasu.md`, branches 1 to 4 and Standards.
- `app/apps/api/src/worker.ts`.


##### .mahou/wiki/api.md
# kurasu: API shape

verified: 2026-10-19

Answers how kurasu's HTTP API is laid out: what is a route, what is a filter, and what travels inside a resource.

## Knowledge

- Each resource has one endpoint, never nested: `/api/<resource>` and `/api/<resource>/{id}`. The one exception is a resource's binary content, at `/{id}/file` (`GET /api/materials/{id}/file`).
- The student uses `/api/<resource>` and the teacher `/api/admin/<resource>`; each side gets only the operations it needs.
- The id of another resource goes in as a filter (`?sessionId=`) or in the body, never in the path.
- A resource includes the values that belong to it: the student's vote is a field of the poll (`myResponse`) and of the question (`myVote`), set with a `PATCH` on that resource.
- A list returns a summary and the detail returns the full resource (`SessionSummary` and `Session`).
- Actions that are not resources, such as requesting a login link or opening a session, stay as actions under `/api/auth/`.
- A malformed teacher request answers a typed 400 and stores nothing: `InvalidPollContent` for poll content of another type (options outside `choice`, scale labels outside `scale`) and `InvalidUpload` for a multipart upload whose fields come after the file or do not decode. Changing the access of a user id that does not exist answers `UserNotFound` (404).
- Every endpoint behind the login also answers the access middleware's errors (requesting a link and opening a session have no middleware): `Unauthenticated`, `NoAccess`, and `NotTeacher` on `/api/admin`.

## Sources

- `.scratch/aula-virtual/program-design/kurasu.md`, branches 3 and 4.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/tasks.md`, T18; test design rows A71, A74 and A91.


##### .mahou/wiki/fence.md
# kurasu: checks and tests

verified: 2026-10-26

Answers which checks reject code in kurasu and where its tests live.

## Knowledge

- oxlint runs type-aware with every rule as an error; oxfmt formats the code.
- A local plugin enforces boundaries: `apps/web` imports only `@kurasu/contract` and `@kurasu/slides` among the project's packages; `packages/core` imports no Cloudflare, Alchemy, Drizzle or jose; `packages/*` never import `apps/*`.
- TypeScript rules: `== null` instead of `=== null` or `=== undefined`; no enums (a const map and a derived type); named exports only.
- The tsconfig compiles with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: an optional prop `?: T` rejects an explicit `undefined`. A prop every caller writes is required and typed `T | undefined`; a prop callers may omit is `?: T | undefined`.
- React rules: arrow-function components with a `Props` interface; React imported by name; conditional rendering with a ternary, never `&&`; no nested ternaries; one component per file; no destructured `useQuery` or `useMutation`.
- The project copies anti-slop into `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/` and adapts it as its own, with its generic and Effect rules.
- `@effect/tsgo` makes `tsc` fail on Effect diagnostics: missing services, `any` in error channels, global `Date`, `fetch` or `console` inside Effect.
- lefthook runs check on every commit; nobody commits with `--no-verify`. The tests run by hand with `pnpm test` before handing work over, because the API suite takes about a minute. turbo caches each package's tests until the package or one of its workspace dependencies changes.
- Tests are integration tests only, in `apps/api/test` (Alchemy's `alchemy/Test/Vitest` in dev mode, HTTP and WebSocket against the local stack) and `apps/web/test` (screens with the real router, the API answered by MSW, Testing Library on happy-dom). Tests live only there: the `test-location` lint rule rejects a test file anywhere else, and the root `projects` list names only the two apps. Before a package whose logic is too complex to cover through the API or the web gets its own tests, extend both the `test-location` rule and the root `projects` list to include it. Tests do not mock modules.
- Two web test helpers control when the mock server answers a request and what it answers. `heldResponse(method, path)` (`test/helpers/held-response.ts`) holds every request to the path until the test calls `release`, so the test can check the screen while the request is still waiting: a skeleton, a pending button. Released without a response, the requests fall through to the handlers already in place. `failingRoute(method, path, status = 500)` (`test/helpers/failing-route.ts`) answers the path with that status and a body no endpoint declares, as a failing server does.
- Pass the handlers that replace the page's own as the `overrides` argument of the test file's `openPage`, which calls `server.use` with them after the page's handlers and before the page renders. If the test calls `server.use` after the page opens, the requests that the page sends while it loads have already reached the page's handlers.
- On a machine under heavy load, some `/aula` tests can run past the 1 s that Testing Library's `findBy*` and `waitFor` wait by default. Run them again before changing them.
- Each API test file deploys its own stage: an empty D1 and R2, the migrations, and its fixtures loaded with `importFiles`. The tests in a file share that database, so each test uses its own records. The test stage sets `allowedDestinationAddresses` to the fixtures' emails; a link requested for an email outside the list makes the mail fail. A test reads the mail bodies from the files the local binding writes under `.alchemy/local/email`, and the sender, recipients and subject from the line the binding logs to the stage's Worker log under `.alchemy/log/<stage>/Api` (`test/helpers/sent-mail.ts`); see `alchemy/local-tests`.
- `app/vitest.config.ts` lists the two projects under Vitest 5's `projects` option; there is no `vitest.workspace.ts`. `happy-dom` and `msw` are also installed at the root, so the whole workspace resolves a single copy of vitest.
- The API project runs at most 4 test files at once (`maxWorkers: 4`): more stages starting together overload the local runtime and every file times out. Each run adds about 130 MB to `apps/api/.alchemy` (see `alchemy/local-tests`).
- The 101 MB upload test (A89) is skipped: under a full run the local runtime sometimes drops the connection mid-upload (EPIPE), and in production Cloudflare cuts a body past 100 MB before it reaches the Worker.
- There are no end-to-end tests. Rows marked `test + manual` in the test design are also run by hand with agent-browser against the local stack (`alchemy dev` and Vite).

## Sources

- `.scratch/aula-virtual/program-design/kurasu.md`, branch 9 and Standards.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/research-tests-alchemy.md`.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/research-stack-local.md` and `.scratch/aula-virtual/test-design/kurasu.md`.
- `app/lefthook.yml`, `app/turbo.json`, `app/vitest.config.ts`, `app/apps/api/vitest.config.ts`, `app/apps/api/test/materials.test.ts`.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/implement/report-refactor.md` (T20).
- `app/apps/web/test/helpers/held-response.ts`, `failing-route.ts`, `app/apps/web/test/admin-classroom.test.tsx`.

- A change to how a part of the app works → a note in `docs/architecture/`

content.thinking:
Fast track is on, so I'll go ahead with this large task of laying out the whole program design tree on the canvas at once. First I need to gather the remaining facts: the Sheet and modal components in the UI, Avatar, PollStateActions, and any test helpers, along with the mockups in the scratch canvas folder, the prototype content, the changelog, and the schema test.

I'm checking whether the schema test pins the enum on the `type` column, since a TS-only enum change may not need a SQL migration. Then I'll sketch the design tree, with the vote endpoint as one of its branches.

I'm weighing whether the counts query needs changing for feedback: its value column holds both the pick and the free text, so grouping by the whole JSON would split tallies by text and leak texts into counts. My leaning is to project only the pick for feedback, so the tally reuses the existing scale bars.

I'm weighing a new admin endpoint for the teacher's response list, either as its own resource filtered by poll id or embedded in the admin poll read, and I'm checking the docs on how responses get joined with users.

I'm settling on where the teacher's response list should live: a separate admin endpoint filtered by poll id, rather than embedding every text in the admin poll read. The modal only opens on demand, so keeping the texts out of the regular poll list seems sensible, and it matches the convention of filtering a resource by another resource's id.

I'm settling on the admin responses as their own resource, named `responses`, with each item carrying the id, the user with name and avatar, the pick, and the text when present, ordered by response id. The main open question is whether that list should paginate or stay bounded, since the cohort is only around thirty students but the wiki says lists paginate by key.

I'm weighing whether the list of responses should be paginated or simply bounded, since the wiki asks for bounded reads but the existing join for raised-in has no limit. I'll leave that as an open question for the user. I'm also checking what the endpoint should answer when the poll isn't a feedback poll, since the item shape requires a pick and a text-free choice response wouldn't fit it.

I'm picking the student-side branch next: a feedback form inside the poll view, with a choice about whether `VoteForm` should branch on the poll type or whether the poll list should pick a separate body, since three places render `VoteForm` today.

I'm checking how `StudentClassroom` renders polls, since the simplest route is to have `VoteForm` return a feedback form early for feedback polls, just as it already branches on word polls, so the callers stay unchanged. For closed feedback polls the student never sees results, so the closed card needs its own body showing their own answer.

I'm checking how the poll meta line should read for feedback, since students never receive results, so the count shouldn't show. I'll look at the prototype's wording for open, answered, and closed states. I'm also planning a shared emoji constant for feedback, used by both the student and teacher sides, and reusing the existing mutation with the error shown inline rather than as a toast.

I'm laying out the teacher side now: the feedback card will show the tally bars with emojis and a button that opens a responses sheet, which will use a `useFeedbackResponses` query hook. The poll menu gains a "Feedback" type, its label gets added, and the editor only needs the prompt field, the same as for words.

I'm checking how the teacher-side responses list gets invalidated when a classroom notice fires, so the query key needs to sit under the admin polls prefix. I'll look at how the invalidation helper matches keys and whether the prototype's button and modal title copy is set.

I'm checking the invalidation helper to see whether the responses key needs the session id in it, and I'm checking whether the database migrations include a snapshot that would change when the feedback enum is added to the schema.

I'm settling on how the feedback tally should be shaped: a dedicated `feedback` key with five counts, one per pick, rather than reusing the `scale` key, since the naming would otherwise be misleading.

Next I'm checking how the API handlers and the worker register the new responses group, and whether the changelog needs an entry.

Fast track is on, so I'm laying out the program design tree and then drawing it on canvas. It's a big job, so I'm settling the plan first. Opening steps come first: one repo, the app/ monorepo, on a clean main, with design.md and the docs notes from commit 9f078a3 as the source.

I'm checking the feedback poll rules next: a feedback poll's results always come back null, and a non-null response just means the student already answered, so I'm working out how the Poll contract should represent that.

I'm weighing how to lay out the GET /polls and PATCH /polls/:id work as one branch, since both run through the same student-side logic. On the teacher side, creating a feedback poll already passes the current fitsType check, so the only real change there is the tally, which needs its own feedback case instead of falling through to the words branch.

I'm deciding how feedback results should be shaped for the teacher: either a new `feedback` key in PollResults or reusing the existing `scale` field. I'm also checking the countRows query, since it groups by the whole value JSON and feedback texts would make every response its own group, so the tally has to aggregate by pick instead.

I'm switching the feedback tally's count query to strip the free-text field out of each response value, so responses group by pick instead of each becoming its own row. The admin side also needs a way to list who answered and what they picked, so I'm weighing a separate responses resource under admin filtered by poll, rather than nesting it inside the poll record.

I'm weighing whether to embed the response list inside the teacher's poll result or expose it through its own lazily loaded endpoint, since the modal only needs it on click. Either fits the docs. I also need to block this listing for choice polls, so it can't reveal who picked what.

I'm weighing whether to have the teacher's feedback responses come through a separate admin endpoint, or to fold them into the poll result. I've got enough context now, so the next step is the program design. I'll lay out the whole tree at once, settle whatever follows from the artifacts and code, and only ask about the open decisions. The repo is on main and clean, and the design notes in the architecture docs are the source. I'll skip the waits and draft the design record before drawing it on the canvas.

I'm working out the feedback poll's effect on the vote endpoint: a new feedback branch in the response contract, and results returned as null for those polls so a student only sees that they already answered.

I'm working out the data-shape details for the feedback poll: the text field stays optional with no length cap, so the program design needs a rule for what happens when the student sends an empty string, whether the key gets dropped or the value gets rejected.

I'm weighing whether an empty text string should be dropped or rejected. The note says an empty text still saves the point alone, so the core should omit it, and whitespace-only text would be stored as typed, which may leave a blank-looking comment for the teacher.

I'm checking how the feedback poll's results will be counted: the grouping query would split each distinct text into its own bucket, so the tally needs to be rebuilt by pick value instead.

I'm weighing how the teacher's results should show the feedback tally: either reuse the `scale` array, so each pick is counted and drawn as a bar, or add a separate key. Reusing `scale` seems right, though the emoji labels under the bars would need to change for feedback.

I'm checking the counts query next: it groups by the full stored value, which for feedback would include each comment's text, so the fix is to strip the text out of the value before grouping so the teacher-side tally stays purely aggregate.

I'm settling how the teacher's feedback tally should be counted, and I'm leaning toward wrapping the counts query so that it strips the text from each feedback value before grouping, keeping the counts purely aggregate, as the data-access notes describe. Whether to reuse the `scale` key for the feedback tally or add a separate key is still open, and I'm weighing that next.

I'm now listing the student-side changes: the list endpoint will always return results as null for feedback polls, while still setting the student's own response, and I'll treat that as one branch together with the answer endpoint. For the teacher's view, I'm considering a separate endpoint for the list of responses, but the API conventions say each resource gets one endpoint and no nesting, so I'd filter by poll id instead.

I'm now deciding whether the teacher's responses endpoint should accept only feedback polls, since other poll types keep individual votes private. A filter by poll id fits the API conventions, but I still need to pick what error a non-feedback poll should return.

I'm weighing whether the teacher's responses endpoint should answer a non-feedback poll with a 404 PollNotFound, a typed 400 error, or an empty list, since other poll types keep individual votes private. I'll settle the route as `/admin/responses?pollId=` in its own group, following the raised-hands pattern.

I'm settling where the teacher's responses endpoint lives: a new `responses.ts` contract file with its own admin group, following the one-file-per-resource convention. On the core side I'm adding a listing method to the Polls service that reads through a store query joining users and ordering by response id.

I'm checking whether the repository's list queries apply a default maximum page size, since the raised-hands listing has no bound and the wiki says lists should be bounded.

I'm moving on to the web side now: the student card on the home and classroom screens, where feedback polls need a comment form in place of the vote form, and the closed-polls card that has to show the student's own answer since results come back null.

I'm settling the feedback poll's closed state on the web side: the closed card will show the student's own answer as its body, since results come back null for feedback polls. I'll add a meta line for feedback polls that says it's editable while open and closed once it shuts.

I'm settling the feedback poll's icon on the web card: the prototype uses a speech bubble, so I'll switch the icon to the chat one when the poll is feedback, while the other poll types keep the chart. The unvoted badge on the classroom side already counts feedback polls, so I'll leave that alone.

I'm settling how the feedback form behaves inside the vote form: it keeps local state for the pick and text, starts from the student's own answer when they choose to edit, and on failure shows an inline error while keeping what they typed. Cancelling an edit goes back to the answered state and drops the draft.

I'm checking how the feedback form's six states map onto the UI, and the closed state is handled by ClosedPolls instead, so a shared FeedbackAnswer component will cover both the answered view and the closed card.

I'm drafting the teacher-side admin poll card next.

I'm wiring the teacher side next: feedback polls get the prompt-only editor like words polls, a "Feedback" type label in the new-poll menu, and a feedback branch in the results bars that shows a face under each bar. There's also a "Ver las respuestas" action that opens a sheet listing each student's name, comment and face, fed by a feedback-responses query.

I'm settling where the "Ver las respuestas" button goes: the teacher's card gets it on feedback polls that are no longer drafts, while drafts keep their usual actions. The panel only shows bars through the shared results view, so I'm leaving it without the button.

I'm weighing the teacher card's action row: the prototype puts "Ver las respuestas" before Borrar and Cerrar, but the current slots render delete first, so I'm considering a new leading slot on PollActions to get that order.

I'm settling the teacher's "Ver las respuestas" button placement: I'll add a leading slot to PollActions so the button sits before Borrar, matching the prototype's order instead of reusing the existing draft slot.

I'm setting up the feedback responses button and its sheet: the button owns the open state, and the sheet only fetches the list once it's opened. I'll title the sheet from the poll's response count, and render the list rows inline in the sheet rather than as a separate component.

I'm checking whether the feedback responses query should be keyed by poll id alone, since the teacher's open sheet wouldn't refresh when a student answers unless the key ties into the session-scoped polls invalidation.

I'm checking whether the responses query key gets invalidated when a student answers, since the sheet should refresh live. Tying it to the session-scoped polls key would catch that, and the optimistic patch in the update hook looks harmless because the response ids never match the poll id.

I'm weighing whether the responses query should be keyed so that it refreshes when students answer, and I'm leaning toward a key that includes the session and poll ids so the polls invalidation can reach it.

I'm settling the last part of the teacher's results view: the feedback bars will get faces under them and their own anchor labels, following the existing scale branch. I also need to decide whether the open responses list should refresh live, and I'm leaning yes so it stays consistent with the bars and the count in the title.

I'm moving on to the student-side closed view for feedback polls, where the closed card should show their answer instead of results, and the poll meta line should say "Encuesta de feedback · cerrada" rather than counting responses.

I'm checking the student-side filter next: feedback polls should be left out of the shown list unless they're closed or the student already answered, and their results come back null. On the admin side, the feedback tally will be built as a count-and-scale shape, and the validation for picks needs to accept a `pick` value instead of the scale or words shapes.

I'm mapping out the responses store query next: it'll join each response to its author and sort by id, so the feedback list comes back in the order students answered.

I'm weighing whether the response contract can reuse the raised-hands user shape for the feedback list, or whether that means pulling a shared type out of another file.

I'm settling the response contract next: the feedback value shape gets pulled out as its own schema, and the author summary gets shared with the raised-hands listing so both use one user type. On the core side the teacher's responses listing checks the poll is a feedback poll and then pulls the responses joined to their authors, and I still need to pick the error for non-feedback polls. The new handler goes in a responses file, with the group and the worker wired up, and the teacher route is already covered by the admin middleware.

I'm checking how the other API resources are laid out and whether the list queries cap their page size, since the teacher's responses listing shouldn't come back unbounded.

I'm weighing three open questions before drafting: whether a whitespace-only comment should count as no text, whether a non-feedback poll should return a 404 or a typed 400 or an empty list, and whether the new list endpoint needs a page-size cap like the others.

I'm checking whether the repository caps page sizes on its list queries, and then I'll look at the drizzle snapshot for any enum on the poll type before I write the design record and start drawing the canvas.

I'm laying out the teacher's poll card and its responses sheet next: the card needs a "Ver las respuestas" button on feedback polls that aren't drafts, and I'll work out the component tree, state, interfaces, and module list for that screen, along with the standards.

I'm laying out the remaining canvas pieces now: the class diagram, the derivation of critical behaviour, the screen mockups, the component tree and state, and the standards flowchart.

I'm checking the page-size limits on the list queries, the drizzle snapshot for a poll type enum, and the icon on the poll card before drafting the record.

# Diseño del programa · kurasu (feedback de una sesión)

Repositorio: este repositorio (`/home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course`), con el monorepo de kurasu en `app/`, en `main` y sin cambios sin commitear. Cubre las seis ramas de `../design.md` y la nota `app/docs/architecture/feedback-de-sesion.md` con las notas que actualizó (commit `9f078a3`). Deja afuera los casos de prueba y las validaciones manuales (`mahou:test-design`).

Fuente: `../design.md`, `app/docs/architecture/feedback-de-sesion.md`, `../prototypes/feedback.html` y `../prototypes/teacher-feedback.html`.

## Árbol

```

   │  ✓ PollType suma "feedback" en el contract y en el enum de la columna (design.md, rama 1)
   │  ✓ Sin migración: la columna type es text sin CHECK y el snapshot no guarda el enum (sigue de 0003_changelog_and_ids)
   │  ✓ fitsType no cambia: el feedback no lleva opciones ni textos de escala, igual que la word cloud (sigue de fits-type.ts)
   │  ✓ ResponseValue suma { pick: 1..5, text?: string } (design.md, rama 1)
   │  ✓ PollResults suma feedback: cinco conteos, uno por punto (sigue de una clave por tipo en PollResults)
   ├─ 2 PATCH /polls/:id · la respuesta del alumno                                                       settled
   │  ✓ fitsPoll acepta en una encuesta de feedback solo un valor con pick (design.md, rama 3)
   │  ✓ Polls.vote guarda el valor sin la clave text cuando text llega vacío (feedback-de-sesion.md, "puede ir vacío o faltar")
   │  ✓ La encuesta de feedback vuelve con results null, abierta o cerrada (decisiones D13)

   ├─ 4 GET /admin/responses · la lista del profe                                                        open

   │  ✓ ClosedPolls pone FeedbackAnswer en el cuerpo de un feedback cerrado, porque no tiene resultados (sigue de D13)
   │  ✓ PollCard elige el ícono por tipo: chat-messages para el feedback (prototypes/feedback.html)

## Lo que el diseño deja para el programa

- La forma de la rama de feedback en `ResponseValue` y la de su conteo en `PollResults`.
- Si hace falta migración para el tipo nuevo.
- Dónde se saca el texto vacío y dónde se niegan los resultados al alumno.
- Cómo la query de conteos cuenta los puntos sin leer los textos.
- El endpoint de la lista con nombres: su ruta, su forma, su orden, su tope y qué responde para otro tipo de encuesta.
- En qué componentes entra la tarjeta del alumno sin tocar a cada pantalla que muestra encuestas.
- Dónde va "Ver las respuestas", qué pieza abre la lista y cómo se refresca.

## 1 POST /admin/polls · el tipo feedback

Parte que se saltea: el callstack, porque crear una encuesta de feedback recorre el mismo camino que una word cloud y solo cambia el literal del tipo. La rama es el modelo compartido que usan las demás.

### 1.1 Class diagram · settled

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class PollType:::changed {
        +"choice" | "words" | "scale" | "feedback"
        <<Schema.Literals, contract>>
    }
    class FeedbackValue:::added {
        +number pick
        +string text
        <<rama de ResponseValue; pick entero 1 a 5; text optionalKey, sin tope>>
    }
    class PollResults:::changed {
        +number[] feedback
        <<optionalKey, cinco enteros como scale>>
    }
    class polls_type:::changed {
        +text type
        <<enum de drizzle solo en TS, sin CHECK, sin migración>>
    }
```

Como las otras ramas, es un `Schema.Struct` sin clave de tipo: la rama se reconoce por la presencia de `pick`. `text` es `Schema.optionalKey(Schema.String)`, así que una respuesta sin texto no lleva la clave y una con texto vacío decodifica y llega al core, que la saca (2.3).

`PollResults.feedback` sigue a `PollResults.scale`: cinco enteros, uno por punto. La columna `polls.type` es `text` sin `CHECK` desde `0003_changelog_and_ids/migration.sql:74` y el snapshot de drizzle no guarda el enum, así que sumar el literal en `schema.ts:85` no genera migración. `GET /api/polls` llega a `forStudent` por `Polls.listForStudent` con las encuestas de la sesión, así que el inicio, el aula y las cerradas del alumno reciben el feedback con `results: null` por el mismo cambio. # Diseño del programa · kurasu (feedback de una sesión)

Repositorio: este repositorio (`/home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course`), con el monorepo de kurasu en `app/`, en `main` y sin cambios sin commitear. Cubre las seis ramas de `../design.md` y la nota `app/docs/architecture/feedback-de-sesion.md` con las notas que actualizó (commit `9f078a3`). Deja afuera los casos de prueba y las validaciones manuales (`mahou:test-design`).

Fuente: `../design.md`, `app/docs/architecture/feedback-de-sesion.md`, `../prototypes/feedback.html` y `../prototypes/teacher-feedback.html`.

## Árbol

```

   ├─ 2 PATCH /polls/:id · la respuesta del alumno                                                       settled

## Lo que el diseño deja para el programa

- La forma de la rama de feedback en `ResponseValue` y la de su conteo en `PollResults`.
- Si hace falta migración para el tipo nuevo.
- Dónde se saca el texto vacío y dónde se niegan los resultados al alumno.
- Cómo la query de conteos cuenta los puntos sin leer los textos.
- El endpoint de la lista con nombres: su ruta, su forma, su orden, su tope y qué responde para otro tipo de encuesta.
- En qué componentes entra la tarjeta del alumno sin tocar a cada pantalla que muestra encuestas.
- Dónde va "Ver las respuestas", qué pieza abre la lista y cómo se refresca.

---

## 1 POST /admin/polls · el tipo feedback

Parte que se saltea: el callstack, porque crear una encuesta de feedback recorre el mismo camino que una word cloud y solo cambia el literal del tipo. La rama es el modelo compartido que usan las demás.

### 1.1 Class diagram · settled

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class PollType:::changed {
        +"choice" | "words" | "scale" | "feedback"
        <<Schema.Literals, contract>>
    }
    class FeedbackValue:::added {
        +number pick
        +string text
        <<rama de ResponseValue; pick entero 1 a 5; text optionalKey, sin tope>>
    }
    class PollResults:::changed {
        +number[] feedback
        <<optionalKey, cinco enteros como scale>>
    }
    class polls_type:::changed {
        +text type
        <<enum de drizzle solo en TS, sin CHECK, sin migración>>
    }
```

`FeedbackValue` es la cuarta rama de la unión `ResponseValue` (`packages/contract/src/polls.ts:63`), al lado de `choice`, `scale` y `words`. Como las otras ramas, es un `Schema.Struct` sin clave de tipo: la rama se reconoce por la presencia de `pick`. `text` es `Schema.optionalKey(Schema.String)`, así que una respuesta sin texto no lleva la clave y una con texto vacío decodifica y llega al core, que la saca (2.3).

`PollResults.feedback` sigue a `PollResults.scale`: cinco enteros, uno por punto. La columna `polls.type` es `text` sin `CHECK` desde `0003_changelog_and_ids/migration.sql:74` y el snapshot de drizzle no guarda el enum, así que sumar el literal en `schema.ts:85` no genera migración. Los `decode` de `D1Polls` y `D1Responses` usan los mismos schemas del contract, así que leen el tipo y la rama nuevos sin cambios propios.

### 1.2 Interfaces y module list · settled

```json
{
  "title": "PollType",
  "$comment": "exists",
  "enum": ["choice", "words", "scale", "feedback"],
  "description": "El tipo de la encuesta; feedback se suma al final."
}
```

```json
{
  "title": "ResponseValue",
  "$comment": "exists",
  "oneOf": [
    { "$comment": "unchanged", "title": "choice" },
    { "$comment": "unchanged", "title": "scale" },
    { "$comment": "unchanged", "title": "words" },
    {
      "$comment": "added",
      "title": "feedback",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "pick": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 5, "description": "El emoji elegido, como número de 1 a 5." },
        "text": { "type": "string", "description": "El comentario, tal como lo escribió. Ausente cuando no escribió nada." }
      },
      "required": ["pick"]
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "title": "PollResults",
  "$comment": "exists",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "feedback": { "$comment": "added", "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 5, "maxItems": 5, "description": "Cuántos eligieron cada punto, del 1 al 5." }
  }
}
```

```
app/packages/
├── contract/src/
│   └── polls.ts                         touched   PollType, ResponseValue y PollResults
├── core/src/polls/
│   └── fits-type.ts                     sin cambios: el feedback ya cae en la regla de la word cloud
└── database/src/
    └── schema.ts                        touched   "feedback" en el enum de polls.type
app/packages/database/migrations/        sin migración nueva
```

## 2 PATCH /polls/:id · la respuesta del alumno

### 2.1 Callstack · settled

```
 PATCH /api/polls/:id                                                       [[app/apps/api/src/handlers/polls.ts#PollsHandlers.vote]]
-given { myResponse: choice | scale | words }
+given { myResponse: choice | scale | words | { pick, text? } }             ← la rama nueva decodifica en el contract
 │
 └─ Polls.vote(viewer, id, response)                                        [[app/packages/core/src/polls/polls.ts#Polls.vote]]
    ├─ when viewer.role is not student → NotStudent (403)
    ├─ findPoll(id) → PollNotFound (404)                                    [[app/packages/core/src/polls/polls.ts#findPoll]]
    ├─ visibleSession(sessions, poll.sessionId) → PollNotFound (404)        [[app/packages/core/src/sessions/visible-session.ts#visibleSession]]
    ├─ when poll.status is not active → PollNotActive (409)
-   ├─ fitsPoll(poll, response) → InvalidResponse (400)                     [[app/packages/core/src/polls/tally.ts#fitsPoll]]
+   ├─ fitsPoll(poll, response) → InvalidResponse (400)    ← feedback acepta solo { pick }   [[app/packages/core/src/polls/tally.ts#fitsPoll]]
+   ├─ value = response.text is "" ? { pick } : response    ← saca el texto vacío
    ├─ crypto.randomULID                                                     id nuevo, solo lo usa el primer insert
-   ├─ responses.upsert({ id, pollId, userId, value: response }, target (pollId, userId))
+   ├─ responses.upsert({ id, pollId, userId, value }, target (pollId, userId))   ← reemplaza value y conserva el id
    ├─ classroom.notify(poll.sessionId, "polls")                            [[app/packages/core/src/polls/polls.ts#notifyPolls]]
    ├─ changelog.drop({ type: "poll-opened", entityId: poll.id })
    └─ forStudent(viewer, [poll])                                           [[app/packages/core/src/polls/polls.ts#forStudent]]
       ├─ responses.list(where userId, pollId)                               myResponse
-      ├─ shown = polls closed or answered
+      ├─ shown = polls not feedback and (closed or answered)  ← el feedback nunca entra
       ├─ responses.counts(shown)
       └─ Poll { …, myResponse, results: shown ? tally(…) : null }           feedback: results null
```

`GET /api/polls` llega a `forStudent` por `Polls.listForStudent` con las encuestas de la sesión, así que el inicio, el aula y las cerradas del alumno reciben el feedback con `results: null` por el mismo cambio. La regla: el alumno manda un punto y quizás un texto, la API lo acepta solo en una encuesta de feedback activa, guarda el texto tal como vino salvo que esté vacío, y nunca le devuelve resultados de un feedback.

### 2.2 Interfaces y module list · settled

```json
{

  "$comment": "exists",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "input": {

├── polls.ts                             touched   texto vacío en vote; el feedback fuera de shown en forStudent
└── tally.ts                             touched   rama feedback en fitsPoll
app/apps/api/src/handlers/
└── polls.ts                             sin cambios: pasa myResponse tal como llega
```

### 2.3 Comportamiento crítico · settled

El texto vacío se saca en `Polls.vote`, después de `fitsPoll` y antes del `upsert`, y no en el schema del contract. Así el contract sigue describiendo lo que viaja, como las otras ramas, y la regla "vacío o ausente se guarda igual" vive en un solo lugar. El texto con espacios se guarda con sus espacios: el diseño pide no recortar.

Los resultados del alumno se niegan en `forStudent` y no en `tally`: `tally` sigue contando el feedback para el profe (3), y el alumno no ve resultados porque su encuesta nunca entra en `shown`. Como `counts` recibe solo `shown`, la query de conteos tampoco lee respuestas de feedback para el alumno.

## 3 GET /admin/polls · el resumen del profe

### 3.1 Callstack · settled

```
 GET /api/admin/polls?sessionId=                                            [[app/apps/api/src/handlers/polls.ts#AdminPollsHandlers.list]]

    ├─ store.list(where sessionId)
    └─ forTeacher(polls)                                                     [[app/packages/core/src/polls/polls.ts#forTeacher]]
-      ├─ responses.counts(pollIds)                                         [[app/packages/database/src/responses.ts#D1Responses.counts]]
+      ├─ responses.counts(pollIds)                ← agrupa el feedback por pick, sin text   [[app/packages/database/src/responses.ts#D1Responses.counts]]
-      └─ tally(poll, counts)                                               [[app/packages/core/src/polls/tally.ts#tally]]
+      └─ tally(poll, counts)                      ← rama feedback: cinco conteos             [[app/packages/core/src/polls/tally.ts#tally]]
```

`PATCH /api/admin/polls/:id` y `POST /api/admin/polls` devuelven la encuesta por el mismo `forTeacher` y `tally`, así que un feedback recién activado o cerrado vuelve con sus barras. La regla: el profe recibe el total y cuántos eligieron cada punto, y la query que los cuenta nunca lee el texto.

### 3.2 Interfaces y module list · settled

Las formas son las de 1.2: `AdminPoll.results` ya es `PollResults`, que gana `feedback`. `ResponseCounts.values` lleva para el feedback un `ResponseValue` de la rama nueva con solo `pick`.

```
app/packages/
├── core/src/polls/
│   ├── tally.ts                         touched   rama feedback en tally
│   └── responses-store.ts               touched   el comentario de counts nombra los puntos de feedback
└── database/src/
    └── responses.ts                     touched   la columna value de la query de conteos
```

### 3.3 Comportamiento crítico · settled

```
D1Responses.counts(pollIds)                                                  touched
  pollIds  := JSON array of the poll ids                                     arg
  value    := words present  ? null                                          computed
              pick present   ? json_object('pick', value ->> '$.pick')       # sin text, agrupa por punto
              otherwise      ? value                                         # choice o scale, como hoy
  rows     := group by pollId, value; union the words rows as today           database
  returns    Map pollId → { count, values: [{ value, count }], words }        returns

tally(poll, counts)                                                          touched
  votes    := counts.values with pick → [pick - 1, count]                    computed
  returns    { count, feedback: countsOf(5, votes) }                          returns
```

Hoy la query agrupa las respuestas de choice y scale por el JSON entero de `value` (`responses.ts:45`). Con el feedback, el JSON lleva el texto, así que agruparía una fila por comentario y le pasaría los textos al core. La columna `value` de la primera parte del `union` pasa a construir `{ pick }` cuando el valor tiene `pick`, así el feedback agrupa por punto y la query sigue sin devolver textos, como dice `acceso-a-datos.md`.

## 4 GET /admin/responses · la lista del profe

### 4.1 Callstack · open

```
+GET /api/admin/responses?pollId=                                           (AdminResponsesHandlers.list)
+given { pollId }
+│
+└─ Polls.listFeedback(pollId)
+   ├─ findPoll(pollId) → PollNotFound (404)                                [[app/packages/core/src/polls/polls.ts#findPoll]]
+   ├─ when poll.type is not feedback → ❔ Q1
+   └─ responses.feedbackOf(pollId)
+      └─ select responses.id, users.id, users.name, users.avatar, responses.value
+         from responses inner join users
+         where pollId, order by responses.id asc, limit ❔ Q2
+         → decode FeedbackResponse { id, user: { id, name, avatar }, pick, text? }
```

La ruta pasa por `/api/admin`, así que el middleware ya responde `NotTeacher` al alumno. Ningún otro camino llega a `feedbackOf`. La regla: el profe pide las respuestas de una encuesta de feedback y recibe, por cada alumno que respondió, su nombre, su avatar, el punto y el texto si escribió, en el orden de la primera respuesta.

### 4.2 Interfaces y module list · open

## 5 Tarjeta de feedback del alumno · inicio y aula

### 5.1 Screen layout · settled

El prototipo `../prototypes/feedback.html` muestra los seis estados y no cambia en esta rama. El estado que lleva el cambio es "sin responder":

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   [ card de la sesión: título, resumen, links ]          │
│   [ encuestas activas de otros tipos ]                   │
│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ← PollCard
│   │  icon  prompt                                      │ │
│   │  meta                                              │ │ ← pollMeta
│   │  ┌──┐ ┌──┐ ┌──┐ ┌──┐ ┌──┐                          │ │ ← FeedbackScale
│   │  └──┘ └──┘ └──┘ └──┘ └──┘                          │ │
│   │  label            label             label          │ │
│   │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │ ← FeedbackForm
│   │  │  textarea                                    │  │ │
│   │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│   │                                       [ button ]   │ │
│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Enviando: los emojis y el campo se deshabilitan y el botón muestra el spinner. Error: `InlineError` entre el campo y el botón, con lo cargado intacto. Respondido: `FeedbackAnswer` con el emoji, el texto o "Sin comentario.", el agradecimiento y "Cambiar mi respuesta". Editando: el formulario con lo que había mandado, el botón "Modificar feedback" y "Cancelar". Cerrada: `FeedbackAnswer` sin el enlace, o "No respondiste esta encuesta.". La misma tarjeta aparece en el aula, en la pestaña Encuestas, y entre las cerradas del alumno.

### 5.2 Component tree · settled

```
ActivePolls · StudentPollsTab · StudentClassroomSkeleton     sin cambios
└── PollCard                                                 touched
    └── VoteForm                                             touched
        └── FeedbackForm                                     new
            ├── FeedbackScale                                new
            └── FeedbackAnswer                               new

ClosedPolls                                                  touched
└── PollCard                                                 touched
    └── FeedbackAnswer · cerrada                             new
```

**PollCard** elige el ícono del encabezado por el tipo: `chat-messages` para el feedback, `chart-bar` para el resto. Sigue siendo la única tarjeta de los dos lados (wiki web).

**VoteForm** devuelve `FeedbackForm` cuando la encuesta es de feedback, igual que ya separa la word cloud en su propia rama. Así ninguna pantalla que muestra encuestas activas cambia.

**FeedbackForm** muestra el formulario, el estado de gracias y el de edición. Tiene el estado local: si está editando, el punto y el texto. Existe aparte de `VoteForm` porque su formulario tiene dos campos y un botón de envío, y la elección y la escala mandan con un toque.

**FeedbackScale** dibuja los cinco emojis como un `radiogroup` y los tres textos de los extremos. Es una pieza propia porque `FeedbackForm` la usa en el formulario nuevo y en la edición con un punto distinto.

**FeedbackAnswer** dibuja una respuesta mandada: el emoji, el texto o "Sin comentario." y la línea de abajo. Recibe la respuesta, si la encuesta está cerrada y un slot `<action>` para "Cambiar mi respuesta". La usan `FeedbackForm` y `ClosedPolls`.

**ClosedPolls** le pasa a `PollCard` un `body` con `FeedbackAnswer` cuando la encuesta es de feedback, porque esa encuesta no tiene resultados que mostrar.

### 5.3 State · settled

```
FeedbackForm                                                                  new
  poll           := poll                                                      prop
  onClosed       := onClosed                                                  prop
  changing       := useState(false)                                           local
  pick           := useState(poll.myResponse?.pick ?? null)                   form
  text           := useState(poll.myResponse?.text ?? "")                     form
  vote           := useVote({ onSuccess: changing ← false,
                              onError: PollNotActive ? onClosed() })           server
  returns          poll.myResponse != null and not changing
                     └─ FeedbackAnswer ← answer: poll.myResponse, closed: false
                        └─ <action> "Cambiar mi respuesta" ← onClick: changing ← true
                   otherwise
                     ├─ FeedbackScale ← value: pick, onChange: pick ←, disabled: vote.isPending
                     ├─ textarea ← text, disabled: vote.isPending
                     ├─ InlineError
                     │    shown while vote.isError and the error is not PollNotActive
                     ├─ "Cancelar" ← onClick: changing ← false
                     │    shown while poll.myResponse != null
                     └─ Button ← disabled: pick == null, pending: vote.isPending,
                                 label: poll.myResponse != null ? "Modificar feedback" : "Enviar feedback",
                                 onClick: vote.mutate({ pollId, myResponse: { pick, text only when text != "" } })

FeedbackAnswer                                                                new
  answer         := answer                                                    prop     # { pick, text? } o null
  closed         := closed                                                    prop
  action         := action                                                    prop     # slot, ausente en la cerrada
  returns          answer == null
                     └─ "No respondiste esta encuesta."
                   otherwise
                     ├─ feedbackFaces[answer.pick - 1]
                     ├─ answer.text ?? "Sin comentario."
                     ├─ closed ? "La encuesta se cerró." : "Gracias, ya nos llegó tu feedback."
                     └─ action

FeedbackScale                                                                 new
  value          := value                                                     prop
  onChange       := onChange                                                  prop
  disabled       := disabled                                                  prop
  returns          radiogroup "Puntaje de la sesión"
                     ├─ five radios from feedbackFaces ← aria-checked: index + 1 == value, onClick: onChange(index + 1)
                     └─ feedbackAnchors

useVote                                                                       touched
  errorToast     := words or pick in input.myResponse ? undefined : "No se pudo registrar tu voto."
```

`pick` y `text` arrancan de la respuesta guardada, así que "Cambiar mi respuesta" abre el formulario con lo que el alumno mandó. Después de un envío exitoso, `useVote` reemplaza la encuesta en la caché con la que devuelve la API, `changing` vuelve a `false` y la tarjeta muestra `FeedbackAnswer`. "Cancelar" vuelve al estado de gracias sin restaurar `pick` y `text`; el formulario se vuelve a abrir con lo último que el alumno eligió, que no se mandó.

## 6 Tarjeta de feedback del profe · pestaña Encuestas

### 6.1 Screen layout · settled

El prototipo `../prototypes/teacher-feedback.html` muestra la tarjeta y su modal y no cambia en esta rama.

Un borrador de feedback muestra solo la pregunta en el editor, como la word cloud. El panel del aula muestra la misma tarjeta con las barras, sin "Ver las respuestas".

### 6.2 Component tree · settled

```
AdminPollsTab                                    sin cambios
├── NewPollMenu                                  touched
└── AdminPollCard                                touched
    └── PollCard
        ├── <body> PollResults · feedback        touched
        └── <actions> PollActions                touched
            ├── <leading>
            │   └── FeedbackResponsesButton      new
